newsitem.title: USA: NBA-Bulls, Rockets go up 3-1 in playoffs.
newsitem.headline: NBA-Bulls, Rockets go up 3-1 in playoffs.

text.p: The Chicago Bulls and Houston Rockets both moved within one win of their conference finals with road victories Sunday, but neither did it without a scare.

Michael Jordan scored 27 points and Scottie Pippen 26 as the Bulls turned away a late comeback by the Atlanta Hawks for an 89-80 victory and a 3-1 lead in their best-of-seven Eastern Conference semifinals.
The Rockets had to go to overtime and needed 26 points and a 3-pointer with 36 seconds left from rookie Matt Maloney to overcome the SuperSonics 110-106 and go up 3-1 in their Western semis.

In the day's first game, Patrick Ewing had 25 points, 11 rebounds and a key block as the New York Knicks held the Miami Heat scoreless down the final 2:51 for a 77-73 home victory and a 2-1 lead in their best-of-seven series.
Chicago won both games in Atlanta and can close out the series with a home win on Tuesday.

Jordan scored 10 points in the final period, including two free throws and a dunk in the final minute, and had a key steal after the Hawks had sliced a 24-point deficit to 83-80, using a 16-2 run in the last five minutes.
After combining for just 38 points in a Game 3 win, Jordan and Pippen resumed carrying the offensive load for the Bulls, who aren't getting much help from anyone else.
"Scottie played well all day, he was a standout player for us today," Bulls coach Phil Jackson said. "Michael obviously pitched in."

Christian Laettner scored 21 points and Steve Smith and Mookie Blaylock 16 apiece for Atlanta, which shot 27 percent (16-of-60) from the field through three periods and finished at 31 percent (25-of-81).
"We had a lot of good looks at the basket and we missed the shots," Hawks coach Lenny Wilkens said.

Bulls forward Dennis Rodman appears to have lost his starting job. He played just 11 minutes, grabbing one rebound and committing four fouls. He was called for a technical foul early in the fourth quarter and has nine technicals in the playoffs, with at least one in each game.
"It's obvious Dennis can't play many minutes because his foul-to-minute ratio will be 1-to-1, and the rest of us have to take up that slack," Bulls forward Brian Williams said.
"Dennis isn't getting an opportunity to play," said fellow forward Jason Caffey. "They (referees) pretty much hold a microscope to him."
In Seattle, Maloney's eighth 3-pointer provided the 25th and final lead change.
"It was a big shot," said Maloney, the only NBA rookie to start all 82 games this season. "I was really satisfied with the look and I knocked it down."
"Hakeem (Olajuwon) makes a great pass out of a double-team and Maloney made the biggest shot of his life," Rockets coach Rudy Tomjanovich said.

Charles Barkley had 26 points and 15 rebounds for the Rockets, who improved to 3-0 on the road in the playoffs and can advance to the conference finals for the fourth time in six years with a home win in Game 5 on Tuesday. Houston has never defeated Seattle in five previous playoff series.
Barkley scored Houston's first seven points in overtime after missing two free throws with 11 seconds left in regulation that could have sealed it.
"I just blew those," said Barkley. "I just messed up. I felt so bad, I knew I had to do something in overtime. The guys supported me but I just felt like a dog."

Gary Payton had 27 points and 11 assists and Hersey Hawkins added 17 points for defending conference champion Seattle, which is 2-3 in home playoff games. The SuperSonics went scoreless in the final 2:25 of Game 3 and the last 1:51 of Game 4.
"Game 5 is simple," Sonics coach George Karl said. "It's pride and heart. They know us and we know them. It's just playing now."
In New York, Ewing atoned for a turnover with his big block of Tim Hardaway's potential game-tying 3-point attempt with three seconds to go.
The Knicks had a 3-point lead and possession when Ewing was double-teamed, lost the ball, recovered it but fell along the sideline with 13 seconds left.
After a timeout, Miami worked the ball to Hardaway, but Ewing jumped out and blocked the shot.
Ewing corraled the loose ball and was fouled with 1.8 seconds to go. He made one free throw to seal New York's fifth win in six postseason games.
The Knicks went up for good at 76-73 on John Starks' three foul shots with 2:42 to go after Voshon Lenard fouled him on a 3-point attempt.
"We played tough defence down the stretch and that's why those free throws made the difference," Starks said.
"It was a foul," Lenard admitted.
Lenard snapped out of a series-long slump with 22 points and Hardaway added 17 and eight assists for the Heat.
The Knicks held the Heat to 31 points in the second half as two of the NBA's best defensive teams produced the second-lowest scoring game in playoff history.
Game 4 is Monday at New York.
